S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text:
## S1_incident_reporting
Manufacturers must report each thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 72 hours of learning of it, with a supplemental investigation report within 30 days. They must notify affected customers within 5 business days when an incident indicates a credible safety risk to their product or requires customer action. Reports must include known model, event, and corrective-action information; confirmed omissions must be corrected promptly.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: A failure rate above 5% triggers regulator-directed corrective action and retesting; it does not, by itself, automatically bar market placement or require withdrawal. Before purchase, customers must receive the model's test results, including observed failure rate and material limitations. Per-model results must not be publicly published by manufacturers or regulators.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before initial market placement and after material design changes. Results must include sample size and uncertainty and be submitted to the regulator. A failure rate above 5% triggers regulator-directed corrective action and retesting; it does not, by itself, automatically bar market placement or require withdrawal. Regulators may restrict placement or require additional measures where the results and other safety evidence indicate unacceptable risk. Before purchase, customers must receive the model’s test results, including observed failure rate and material limitations. Per-model results must not be publicly published by manufacturers or regulators.

S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text:
## S3_remote_shutoff
New home battery models placed on the market 24 months after adoption must provide a secure remote emergency shut-off capability, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a local means of disconnection. Manufacturers must make a compatible retrofit available for installed units where technically feasible and complete retrofits within 6 years of adoption. Retrofit instructions and limitations must be communicated to affected customers.

parameters.quote: New home battery units manufactured for sale 36 months after adoption of this standard must include built-in fire suppression appropriate to the battery chemistry and installation. Existing installed units are not subject to a retrofit mandate under this section.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New home battery units manufactured for sale 36 months after adoption of this standard must include built-in fire suppression appropriate to the battery chemistry and installation. Existing installed units are not subject to a retrofit mandate under this section.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New home battery units manufactured for sale 36 months after adoption of this standard must include built-in fire suppression appropriate to the battery chemistry and installation. The system must be designed to limit fire propagation and must not create a greater electrical or toxic-exposure hazard. Manufacturers must document validation testing and provide installation, maintenance, and end-of-life instructions to customers and regulators. Existing installed units are not subject to a retrofit mandate under this section.

parameters.quote: A recall is mandatory when a regulator-verified model rate exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. The remedy may include repair, replacement, or another regulator-approved corrective action; recall does not by itself require a permanent market ban.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A recall is mandatory when a regulator-verified model rate exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. The remedy may include repair, replacement, or another regulator-approved corrective action; recall does not by itself require a permanent market ban.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before purchase, customers must receive model-specific thermal-test results, including the test temperature, observed failure rate, sample size, and material limitations; results must also be provided to regulators. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of safety notices, corrective actions, and any instructions needed to reduce risk. A recall is mandatory when a regulator-verified model rate exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. Manufacturers must notify regulators and affected customers without delay and provide a remedy plan. The remedy may include repair, replacement, or another regulator-approved corrective action; recall does not by itself require a permanent market ban. Regulators may require a recall sooner where evidence indicates imminent risk.

judge_section_notes: S2 was converted from a market-placement pass/fail limit into a corrective-action and retesting trigger at 5%, with no sales stop, which mainly protects Northwind's Hearth 10 at 6.2%. S5 keeps a mandatory 8/100k recall that Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9) would trigger, but the remedy can be corrective action rather than a market ban. S3 gives 24 months for new units and an open-ended 'where feasible' retrofit escape, which favours Northwind's low retrofit share, while S4's 36-month suppression mandate matches Halcyon's red line. The transcript contains no Northwind-negotiator messages, so that style rating is low-confidence.
